Describe how to make a pure, dry sample of lead iodide.
Dissolve lead nitrate in distilled water in one beaker
Dissolve potassium iodide in distilled water in another beaker
A bright yellow precipitate of lead iodide forms
Filter the mixture to collect the yellow precipitate
Wash the precipitate with distilled water to remove impurities
Dry in a warm oven or between filter papers

A student wants to test if a solution contains chloride ions. Describe the test.
Add a few drops of dilute nitric acid (to remove carbonate ions that might interfere)
Add a few drops of silver nitrate solution
If chloride ions are present, a white precipitate of silver chloride forms
